was fixed (Hadley fixed it by chance and did not really know why). I
do not have any suggestions other than suppressWarnings()...

On Wed, Nov 14, 2012 at 8:36 AM, massyah <mas...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi!
>
> I was having the same problem as Aaron
> (https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/knitr/nt36wDzzXSA)
> where my ggplots appeared late (offsetted from other R output around them).
> I updated evaluate and knitr using the github repos (As suggested there :
> https://github.com/hadley/evaluate/issues/14 ) and it solved my problems,
> temporary.
>
> It turns out that the same problem appears when you have warnings raised by
> any function in the chunk. For example,
>
> ```{r simpleBadEval,results='asis',warning=FALSE}
> computeSomething <-function(x){
> warning("Computation done")
> }
>
> for(i in 1:5){
> text=paste("Doing plot",i)
> cat("<br>\n####",text,"<br><hr>\n")
> computeSomething(text)
> plot(iris$Petal.Width,iris$Petal.Weight,main=text)
> cat("Finished",text)
> }
>
>
>
> This produces figures and text that are out of sync. The only workaround I
> found was to use suppressWarning around the function call. Is this an issue
> that someone else is facing?
>
> Thanks,
> Sam.

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Late appearance of any plot
parts:
Well, you can actually borrow the idea in the example (construct your
source text manually):
https://github.com/yihui/knitr-examples/blob/master/021-ggplot2-geoms.Rnw

And you can rewrite your document in this way:

```{r test-warning, include=FALSE, tidy=FALSE}

titles = sprintf("Doing plot %s", 1:5)

res = knit(text = paste(sprintf(
"

#### %s ```{r simpleBadEval%s}
computeSomething()
plot(iris$Petal.Width, iris$Petal.Weight, main='%s') ```

Finished %s
", titles, 1:5, titles, titles), collapse = ' '))
```

Now write the results:

`r res`

Regards,
Yihui
